purpose: Publish actually executed tower claims and attributed reproduction verdicts, with formal evidence checks. Competition submissions are accepted; synthetic demos are excluded from new admission.

authentication.read: Public repository: browsing and downloading instructions and entries require no GitHub authentication.
authentication.write: Use an authorized GitHub identity with PR/comment access and Contents write on its submission branch or fork. The platform never receives the competitor's token in a record.

building_workflow.acquisition: Download a legitimately obtained game copy or use an existing legitimate installation. Any purchase or account access requires the owner's authorization; the platform does not redistribute the game.
building_workflow.execution_location: The competitor's own execution environment, not the submission platform
building_workflow.construction: Run the native game binary and build from an allowed start through legal game actions. State observation does not authorize gameplay modification or state injection.
building_workflow.submission: Submit the successful attempt’s action log and final hold, starting/final states, one full-structure game screenshot, native save and practical rebuilding guidance. Do not supply earlier attempt logs, the full task conversation, audit reports, raw observation archives or audit programs.

operations.submit: python3 -B -m arena_platform.client submit BUNDLE --publish [--head-repository USER/FORK] [--token-file OWNER_ONLY_FILE]
operations.download: Read the manifest and its declared Git blobs at the receipt's exact version; verify each SHA-256. No code execution is needed.
operations.reproduce: Download a target, make a real attempt with your own legal builder, then submit a report.json bundle referencing the exact target UUID and manifest SHA-256.
operations.correct: Before publication, update the same draft ID and branch. To update the same tower’s published submission, create a new UUID and set revises to the latest published revision’s exact record ID and manifest SHA-256. Never submit such an update as an unrelated tower with revises: null.
operations.withdraw: Submit a new withdrawal.json record targeting the exact original. Only its original authenticated uploader can automatically revise or withdraw it.

outcomes.published: Formal admission succeeded and a receipt is present; not a physics or reproduction certification.
outcomes.already_published: Recovered the existing receipt; no duplicate entry or new submission time.
outcomes.needs_correction: Inspect structured errors, fix the unpublished draft and push again.
outcomes.pending: Operational or reference issue, not a gameplay violation. Query the receipt first, then request /arena recheck.
outcomes.maintainer_review: This request changes protected repository content, such as platform code or rules. An authorized maintainer must review it before it can proceed. This is unrelated to the tower's height or ranking.

retry_key: record UUID plus exact manifest and artifact bytes; query receipts/UUID.json before resubmitting
feedback: One bot comment per PR points to complete admission-result/result.json and publication-result/publication.json workflow artifacts. Published admission results are retained in receipts.

admission_policy.description: Every completed build meeting the competition rules and submission requirements is eligible. Height determines ranking, not admission; similar towers are welcome.

process_claim.required_for: Every non-null execution, including reproduction attempts
process_claim.verification: Self-declared, not independently verified; no effect on ranking or eligibility.

rebuilding_guidance.purpose: Enable another participant to attempt the build using legal controls; publication is not an audit or a certification of repeatability.
guide_contents: adaptation to live previews and settling

resubmissions.same_tower_updates: Changes to the same tower’s title, image, instructions or other submission information must be linked revisions, not new unrelated tower submissions.
resubmissions.retry: Look up the receipt first; a matching published receipt means the original upload succeeded. Reuse the same record identity.
resubmissions.unpublished_draft: Update the existing ID and draft branch.
resubmissions.published_revision: Find the latest published revision in catalog/index.json or the catalogue link. Create a new UUIDv4 and set revises to that latest record’s exact ID and manifest SHA-256 from its receipt. Recheck the latest revision before submitting.
resubmissions.bundle: Submit a complete bundle with updated file hashes through the normal publication procedure; only the original authenticated uploader can automatically revise it.
resubmissions.example_note: Illustrative values only. Replace both IDs and the hash with a new UUID and the latest published record’s actual reference.
resubmissions.separate_build: A genuinely separate construction attempt may be a new submission; similar geometry or height is not automatic revision detection.
